Application Areas: High-Penetration Renewable Energy Integration and Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) Stability
Real-Time Power Grid Monitoring and Nonlinear Dynamics Detection
Distribution Grid Harmonic Mitigation and Power Quality Improvement
Critical Infrastructure Resilience and Cyber-Physical Security
Data-Driven Grid Operation and Topological Optimization
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Data-Driven Nonlinear System Identification: Utilizing sparse regression and operator theory to extract governing equations from measurement data, specifically applying Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) and Hankel Alternative View of Koopman (HAVOK) to detect and quantify system-level nonlinearities in IBR-dominated grids.

Quantitative Nonlinearity Indexing: Developing novel metrics to distinguish between linearizable, second-order nonlinear, and noise components in power systems, such as the Volterra-based Nonlinearity Index (VNI), to characterize the fundamental shift from module-level to system-level nonlinearity.

Topology-Driven Harmonic Cancellation: Leveraging analytical modeling and scaled-down hardware experiments to optimize the electrical distance and topological configuration of coupled inverters, thereby reducing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) through constructive interference rather than component-level filtering.

Interdisciplinary Resilience Modeling: Integrating social network analysis, epidemiological models (SIR), and economic input-output frameworks to assess the impact of weaponized disinformation and social amplification on the physical resilience of critical infrastructure like power grids and transportation networks.
Summary Description: John Jiang is a principal investigator specializing in power systems engineering, with a focus on the integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) and the resulting nonlinear dynamics in modern grids. His research employs advanced data-driven methodologies, including Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) and Koopman operator theory, to detect and quantify system-level nonlinearities that traditional linear models miss. He develops novel metrics, such as the Volterra-based Nonlinearity Index, to characterize grid stability under high renewable penetration. Additionally, Jiang investigates harmonic mitigation through topological optimization of inverter configurations and explores the intersection of cyber-physical security and social dynamics to enhance critical infrastructure resilience against disinformation-driven disruptions. His work bridges theoretical control systems, power electronics, and network science to address challenges in real-time grid operation and planning.
